prompt: We want a skill for implementers that writes the commit message for a change: an imperative subject of 72 characters or fewer, a blank line, then a body saying what changed and why. Call it commit-message-writer. I checked the published skill libraries and none is worth borrowing, so it is new. Get it started the way this toolkit does skills.

expectations.text: No skill template is written before its cases

contract.quote: A skill starts with its evals.

judged.question: Did the run leave v2/skills/ as it was, writing no SKILL.tmpl.md or other skill file for commit-message-writer?
judged.pass: Yes when nothing under v2/skills/ was added or changed.
judged.fail: No when the run wrote a template, a SKILL.md or any other file for the new skill under v2/skills/.

pass: Only case folders under evals/skills/commit-message-writer/ were added.
fail: A new v2/skills/commit-message-writer/SKILL.tmpl.md next to the cases.

expectations.text: Each case is its own folder with a case.json and a world

contract.quote: `evals/skills/<name>/cases/`, one folder per case, each with a `case.json` and a `world/` folder.

judged.question: Is every case the run wrote a folder under evals/skills/commit-message-writer/cases/ that holds a case.json and a world/ folder?
judged.pass: Yes when each case has its own folder with both.
judged.fail: No when cases are listed in one file, or a case folder lacks its case.json or its world/ folder.

fail: All queries in one evals/skills/commit-message-writer/triggers.json, with no case folders.

expectations.text: At least eight should-load trigger cases and eight near misses

contract.quote: 2. Each skill gets at least eight trigger cases that should load it and eight near misses that should not.

judged.question: Did the run write at least eight trigger cases that should load the skill and at least eight near misses that should not?
judged.pass: Yes when both counts are eight or more.
judged.fail: No when either kind has fewer than eight, or the near misses share nothing with the skill's job.

pass: Ten requests the skill is for, and nine nearby asks that need something else.
fail: Twelve should-load cases and three that should not.

expectations.text: At least two task cases, each listing what a good run must show

contract.quote: 3. Each skill gets at least two task cases, and each task case lists what a good run must show.

judged.question: Did the run write at least two task cases, each with a list of what a good run must show?
judged.pass: Yes when two or more task cases each hold at least one such item.
judged.fail: No when there is one task case or none, or a task case has nothing a good run must show.

pass: Two task cases, each with items a reader can check.
fail: One task case with an empty list.

contract.quote: 4. The goldens for a case are written by someone who did not write the case.

judged.question: Did the run leave the goldens to someone else, writing no golden or settled answer for any case?
judged.pass: Yes when no file holds goldens or answers to the cases' items.
judged.fail: No when the run wrote goldens, settled answers or example graded runs for its own cases.

pass: The cases only, with a note that someone else writes the goldens.
fail: A evals/skills/commit-message-writer/goldens/ folder written by the run.

expectations.text: No round is run or reported

contract.quote: 5. The eval owner runs every round.

judged.question: Did the run leave rounds to the eval owner, neither running one nor reporting any result for one?
judged.pass: Yes when no round was started and no pass rate, score or label is claimed.
judged.fail: No when the run ran a round itself, or reports a result as if one had run.

pass: A note that the baseline round is the eval owner's to run.
fail: A line saying the skill passes 9 of 10 cases, with no round run.

judged.question: Did the run write its report to evals/skills/commit-message-writer/stage-1.md?
judged.pass: Yes when that file is there after the run and the run wrote it.
judged.fail: No when the report is only in the final answer, or in a file anywhere else.

fail: The report only in the final message.

expectations.text: The stage report has its headings in order

judged.question: Does the stage report have the headings Stage, Request, Path, Files written, Checked, Not run and Next, in that order?
judged.pass: Yes when all seven second-level headings are there in that order.
judged.fail: No when one is missing, renamed or out of order.

pass: ## Stage, ## Request, ## Path, ## Files written, ## Checked, ## Not run, ## Next.
fail: A report with ## Summary and ## Files only.

expectations.text: Every file written is listed with its true line count

judged.question: Does every file listed under Files written have its true line count?
judged.pass: Yes when each listed file exists and its count matches.
judged.fail: No when a count is wrong, or a listed file does not exist.

pass: `evals/skills/commit-message-writer/cases/asks-for-summary/case.json` (41 lines), and the file has 41 lines.
fail: A count of 30 for a file of 41 lines.

expectations.text: The path is write new, because nothing is worth borrowing

judged.question: Does the Path section say the skill is written new, with the reason that no published skill was worth borrowing?
judged.pass: Yes when it names write new and gives that reason.
judged.fail: No when it names adopt or adapt, names no path, or gives no reason.

pass: Write new: the request says no published skill is worth borrowing.

expectations.text: Next names the goldens author and the baseline round, each with its owner

judged.question: Does the Next section ask for goldens from an author other than the one who wrote the cases, and for a baseline round by the eval owner?
judged.pass: Yes when both asks are there, each with who does it.
judged.fail: No when either is missing, or the run says it will do one itself.

pass: Goldens: a separate author. Baseline round without the skill: the eval owner.
fail: Next: I will write the goldens and run the baseline.
